nasturtium.region_notes_beginner: In St. George's Dixie, nasturtium is a spring flower, not a summer one. Direct-sow it around April 1 once frost has passed, in poor soil with no fertilizer; it resents being moved, so sow it where it will grow. Leaves and blooms come in about seven weeks, and you can pick leaves, flowers, and green pods to eat through late spring and into June. Once the desert heat sets in for good in July, nasturtium stalls and stops flowering, so plan on the spring crop finishing before summer rather than a second wave in fall. Use it as an aphid trap near your vegetables while it lasts.
